memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Abimelek brought sheep and cattle and male and female slaves and gave them to Abraham, and he returned Sarah his wife to him. And Abimelek said, "My land is before you; live wherever you like." - Gen 20:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Watch the flow of grace in this scene, and notice which direction it runs. Abraham is the one who sinned. He lied, endangered a kingdom, and stood exposed and guilty. And yet Abimelech - the one who was wronged - responds by giving Abraham sheep, cattle, servants, returning his wife, and offering him the freedom to live anywhere in the land. The wronged party lavishes kindness on the wrongdoer.

This is a striking picture of undeserved favour. Abraham deserved rebuke and expulsion; he received gifts and generosity. There is something almost gospel-shaped about it - grace flowing toward the one who least deserved it.

And here is the humbling truth beneath it: God was keeping His promise to bless Abraham even when Abraham was failing. Remember God's word: "I will bless you... and whoever curses you I will curse" (Gen 12:2-3). Even in Abraham's disgrace, God was working to protect and prosper him. God's faithfulness to His promise did not depend on Abraham's faithfulness in the moment.

This is the wonder of grace in our own lives. God often blesses us in seasons when we have least deserved it, keeping His promises when we have broken ours. His steadfast love is not a reward for our performance but a gift flowing from His own faithful character. "If we are faithless, he remains faithful" (2 Tim 2:13). Have you noticed the undeserved kindnesses God has shown you, even in your failures?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where has God shown you undeserved kindness, even in your failures?
- How does God's faithfulness despite your unfaithfulness move your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You bless me even when I least deserve it, keeping Your promises when I break mine. Your grace flows from Your faithful character, not my performance. Thank You for Your undeserved kindness.
Amen.
